div.h2: How Odoo works in your industry
div.p: The same platform, set up around how each kind of business makes money. Here is where we usually start.

article.p: Sales orders drive purchasing and production. Bills of materials, work orders and maintenance keep the shop floor in step with what has been sold, and material and labor costs roll up to show real margins.
Stock across warehouses, reordering rules that buy before you run out, and pricelists for each customer. Picking, packing and shipping run on barcode scans, and invoices go out when goods ship.
Your online store runs on the same products, stock and customers as your back office. Orders go straight to fulfillment, and email campaigns use real purchase history.
From lead to signed quote to delivery: accepted quotes become projects, the team logs time against them, and invoices follow milestones or hours worked.
Jobs scheduled by crew and location, materials drawn from stock, and work signed off on site from a phone. Every job tracks its costs against the quote.

For clinics, care providers and billing companies: appointment booking, intake forms, staff schedules, client communication and billing in one place. Clinical records stay in your specialist system; Odoo runs the business around them.
Donors, volunteers and CSR partners in one CRM. Campaigns, events and programs are tracked with their costs, so every contribution can be accounted for and reported.
Stories published from Odoo’s website builder, subscriptions that renew and invoice themselves, and advertising deals managed in a sales pipeline.

div.p: Some apps, such as Field Service, Quality, Barcode, Planning, Appointments, Helpdesk and Subscriptions, are part of Odoo Enterprise. We tell you what your edition includes before you commit.
